transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-11-19
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam Park (Redwood SE), Dr. Anika Rao (CTO - Spectral), Miguel Santos (ML Eng), Raj Patel (Infra), Sara Lim (Product)
Links shared: deck: https://redwood.app/decks/model-selection, security pack: https://redwood.app/security/spectral, benchmark sheet: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/spectral-template

Summary (auto): High-level discovery focused on model selection for Spectral's multi-lingual clinical summarization product. Main tradeoffs discussed: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, context windows (8k vs 32k+), tool-calling support, latency SLOs, cost estimates and security/KMS needs. Agreed next steps: send TCO spreadsheet, benchmarking template, customer to provide sample prompts and security requirements.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um uh I'm Maya from Redwood, AE on this account, and then Liam from the infra side will help with the deep technicals.
[00:06] Anika: Hi all, Anika here — CTO at Spectral. We are evaluating options for model selection. Main ask: accurate clinical summarization across English, Spanish, Portuguese and occasional Chinese, and we need tool-calling for our structured extraction pipelines.
[00:18] Liam: Great. Quick intro from me, Liam Park, Redwood SE. We usually look at model accuracy, context length, token cost, and whether the model supports tool-calling / function calling out of the box.
[00:28] Miguel: Yep, hi, Miguel. We have transcripts and device logs that can be long — some patient encounter threads go 20k tokens easily, so context length matters. Also multilingual quality is critical.
[00:40] Raj: And from infra: we'll need SOC2, KMS integration, SSO SAML, and likely a VPC/private deployment for PHI. Curious differences between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private here.
[00:52] Maya: Perfect — that's the typical checklist. For model selection, are you leaning towards an open model or considering managed models like OpenAI?
[00:58] Anika: Preference for open models due to cost and auditability, but we're open. The tie-breaker is latency and the ability to run in our VPC.
[01:06] Liam: On open models, Redwood hosts a catalog of verified open models with performance profiles. For context windows: we have options — some variants we host reach 32k+ context, others are optimized for 8k. There's also approach to chunking plus KV cache to stitch long conversations.
[01:22] Miguel: KV cache? We saw something about KV cache — can you explain how that helps with long docs?
[01:27] Liam: Sure. KV cache stores key/value representations of prior tokens so when you re-invoke a model you don't need to re-encode the whole history. With prefix caching and smart stitching we can effectively handle long sequences without re-sending everything — reduces token cost and latency for repeated context. Sometimes transcription shows that as "KV cash" in quick notes, lol.
[01:43] Anika: Any tradeoffs? Does caching affect real-time summaries?
[01:47] Liam: It can introduce some complexity for strict single-request semantics; for streaming and live edits we keep a small active window and use cache for older history. For clinical summarization where correctness matters, we recommend a 32k context model if you want single-shot summarization; otherwise chunk+stitch with strong overlap and validation works well.
[02:05] Miguel: Regarding model families — which open models give us the best multilingual clinical output? We saw Llama-3 variants, MPT, and Mistral — plus some specialised bio-med models.
[02:15] Maya: Right. Llama-3 style families usually have strong English performance; some fine-tuned variants or instruction-tuned med models can do better for clinical terms. We also surface models like Starcoder variants for code/tooling. Mistral family is competitive, and there's a growing set of med-finetuned checkpoints. The tradeoff is that larger multilingual models or med-finetuned ones can be heavier in latency/cost.
[02:32] Anika: Do you run quantized variants? We need predictable memory footprint and cost.
[02:36] Liam: Yes, Redwood supports quantized runtimes (8-bit, 4-bit variants depending on model). Our runtime chooses kernels and quantized execution paths for efficiency; sometimes 4-bit quant yields 2-3x speed/cost improvements but may impact some rare token probabilities. We'll help run evals on your prompts to pick the best quantization point.
[02:55] Raj: For Private deployment, how tightly do you integrate with our KMS? We have HSM-backed keys and strict key rotation.
[03:02] Maya: In Private (VPC/on-prem) we can integrate with your KMS/HSM and offer customer-managed keys; key material never leaves your environment. We'll also provide audit logs and can scope SOC2 controls.
[03:12] Raj: Good. Also want to confirm SSO and RBAC — can we map roles to internal groups?
[03:17] Liam: Yes, SAML/SSO mapping and RBAC are supported in Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we offer enterprise SSO with scoped roles, but Dedicated gives more isolation.
[03:25] Anika: Latency targets: we need 99th percentile for single-request summarization to be under 1.0s ideally, but realistic — maybe < 1.5s. Is that achievable?
[03:34] Liam: Sub-1s 99th for large models is very tough, generally requires smaller optimized variants or Dedicated GPU pools with lower batch sizes. Our Dedicated customers often hit ~0.6–1.2s with optimized models and small batch sizes on A100/H100 or equivalent. Hosted can achieve low latency but depends on plan and reserved capacity. We'll include expected latency profiles in the TCO sheet.
[03:54] Miguel: We also need tool-calling — specifically a structured JSON output with fields like diagnosis_code, summary, action_items. Do open models support that reliably?
[04:02] Maya: Most instruction-tuned models can do function-calling or structured output with templates. For higher reliability we pair them with a validation/heuristics layer and can offer reranking or a small secondary model to verify fields. Redwood supports function/tool calling primitives in the API so you can route calls to your extraction services.
[04:16] Anika: Multilingual — how do you evaluate Spanish/Portuguese? We need clinical-level accuracy, not just translation.
[04:22] Liam: We'll run evals on your provided prompt set in each language. Some open models are stronger in Romance languages; others need fine-tuning. We also recommend domain-adaptive finetuning or retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) using your clinical KB to boost accuracy.
[04:36] Miguel: Retrieval — do you recommend RAG for long histories?
[04:40] Liam: Yes, RAG + chunking is a good pattern: index encounter notes and use dense retrieval to pull relevant chunks into the prompt. Combine with KV cache for session state. It trades some complexity for robustness at scale.
[04:49] Anika: Security question — data retention in Hosted mode, do you keep logs or user data?
[04:54] Maya: Hosted can be configured to not retain user data past the request; audit logs are available based on retention settings. For PHI, we typically recommend Dedicated or Private to ensure no multi-tenant storage of sensitive content, plus contractual BAA if needed.
[05:06] Raj: Cost — give me a ballpark: if we have 200k tokens per day with 30% being long-context summarizations, what difference is Hosted vs Dedicated?
[05:15] Maya: That's exactly what the TCO sheet will show; rough ballpark: hosted per-token costs are higher but no infra ops, Dedicated reduces per-token cost significantly once you hit steady utilization because of reserved capacity. Private has higher fixed platform fees but gives control and lower marginal costs at very high scale. We'll model your 200k tokens/day usage in the sheet.
[05:34] Miguel: On the subject of benchmarks, can you run our sample prompts against three candidate models and provide accuracy metrics and latency?
[05:40] Liam: Yes — we'll run the benchmarking template. We recommend at least 1k representative prompts across languages to get meaningful metrics. We'll produce confusion matrices for structured fields and token-level cost estimates.
[05:52] Sara: Timeline — we want a pilot in Q1; is that realistic?
[05:56] Maya: Absolutely. Pilot flow: sign MSA/DSAs, dedicated trial capacity for 4–6 weeks, run benchmarks, then decide on Dedicated commit vs Private.
[06:06] Anika: Any limitations with tool-calling and streaming? We occasionally need streaming structured extraction while the model generates — is that supported?
[06:12] Liam: Streaming + tool-calling is available in our runtime; we stream tokens and can emit function call intents mid-stream. There's some care required to handle partial JSON outputs, but our SDKs provide helpers for resilient parsing and retries.
[06:26] Miguel: Are there any known pitfalls with multilingual tokenizers and cost spikes?
[06:30] Liam: Tokenization variance can change token counts across languages — e.g., Chinese may have different token density. We'll surface expected tokenization estimates in the benchmark output. Also we can apply compression techniques or prompt templating to control cost.
[06:44] Anika: For Private, what's the on-prem footprint for a 32k context model?
[06:48] Liam: Depends on quantization. 8-bit or 4-bit quantized variants can fit on 80–160GB GPU memory models often on multi-GPU setups. We'll propose hardware sizing in the Dedicated sizing doc.
[06:59] Raj: Network egress and VPC peering — do you support direct connect / private link?
[07:03] Maya: Yes, for Private deployments we support private connectivity and can work with your cloud provider to set up VPC peering or Direct Connect. Dedicated has options for private endpoints too.
[07:12] Miguel: A small point — model drift and monitoring: how do you alert on regressions?
[07:17] Liam: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets/evals. We can set thresholds and integrate alerts into PagerDuty/Slack.
[07:26] Anika: Okay great. Let's recap real quick.
[07:29] Maya: Recap: 1) We'll send Hosted vs Dedicated/Private TCO and latency profiles; 2) Liam will run benchmark template on 3 candidate models (we propose two Llama-3 variants and one med-finetuned Mistral) using your prompt set; 3) Customer to send sample prompts and compliance/network docs; 4) Schedule follow-up demo for Dedicated sizing (we suggested 2025-11-26).
[07:48] Anika: Sounds good. One last: are there pre-built med-finetuned models in Redwood catalog or we need to fine-tune?
[07:54] Maya: We have some curated med-finetuned variants and partner checkpoints; if you need specialized tuning we can help with a fine-tuning or RLHF engagement.
[07:59] Sara: Thanks everyone, that's helpful.
[08:02] Maya: Thanks all, will follow up with the docs and links.
[08:06] Miguel: Thanks.

End of call.
